candidateAudit.title: 🏗️ Wie stabil ist eigentlich eine Brücke? Und hält das wirklich? Dächer, Brücken und Gebäude müssen stabil sein – schließlich sollen sie uns nicht auf den Kopf fallen! 😄 In unser
candidateAudit.text: 🏗️ Wie stabil ist eigentlich eine Brücke? Und hält das wirklich? Dächer, Brücken und Gebäude müssen stabil sein – schließlich sollen sie uns nicht auf den Kopf fallen! 😄 In unserem Workshop „Hält das auch?“ sind wir diesen Fragen gemeinsam auf den Grund gegangen. Wir haben Statik am eigenen Körper ausprobiert, Belastungstests mit selbstgebauten Modellen durchgeführt und einige Brücken in der Stadt erkundet. Dabei ging es unter anderem über die Pontonbrücke zur Donauinsel und in die Venediger Au, wo wir herausgefunden haben, wie stabil Sandburgen tatsächlich sind. 🏖️ Zurück im Architekturzentrum Wien wurde dann selbst gebaut: Wir konstruierten eigene Brücken im Maßstab 1:1 und lernten das faszinierende Material Lehm kennen. Dabei entstanden auch zwei eigene Lehmziegel – denn dank des Projekts „Creative Earth“ haben wir nun zwei Lehmmodelle im Haus. 🧱🌱 Der Workshop bot jede Menge Raum für Fantasie, räumliches Denken und Teamarbeit und war ideal für neugierige Kinder, die Lust hatten, zu bauen, zu experimentieren und Architektur mit allen Sinnen zu entdecken. Das Projekt „Creative Earth“ wird von der FFG im Rahmen von „Talente regional“ unterstützt.

candidateAudit.title: Do you know what happens to coffee after it is harvested? Before it becomes the bean you know and following the initial processing we already talked about, the coffee cherry must l
candidateAudit.text: Do you know what happens to coffee after it is harvested? Before it becomes the bean you know and following the initial processing we already talked about, the coffee cherry must lose most of its moisture. This is the drying phase, a process that varies depending on how the coffee was processed earlier. In natural (or dry) processing, the whole cherries—with all the pulp still intact around the bean—are spread out on large concrete patios or raised drying beds. They stay here in the sun for two to four weeks. During this time, they must be raked and turned daily to prevent unwanted fermentation that would alter the coffee’s flavor profile. Once they have shed their excess moisture, they are hulled using specialized machinery that separates the bean from the outer skin, pulp, and parchment layer. In washed (or wet) processing, however, the bean reaches the drying stage already clean, having had its skin removed and been washed following fermentation. It is then spread out in the sun or placed in mechanical dryers until it reaches the proper moisture level. A final step removes the parchment. Two different paths, same goal: a stable bean, ready for roasting.

candidateAudit.text: … 🌍 GLOBAL – NEUTRAL. Architektur aus Österreich in Afrika und Asien 1955–1989“ Anne Wübben, Leiterin der Architekturvermittlung nimmt euch mit durch die Ausstellung und gibt einen kurzen Einblick in die Schau und ihre spannenden Geschichten. Die Ausstellung folgt den Spuren österreichischer Architekt*innen, die zwischen 1955 und 1989 in Afrika und Asien tätig waren – in einer Zeit der Dekolonisierung, des Kalten Krieges und neuer internationaler Kooperationen. Pläne, Fotografien und Modelle aus der Sammlung des Az W erzählen von realisierten und visionären Projekten in Ländern wie Indien, Nepal, Tansania, Burkina Faso, Iran oder Kuwait. Sie eröffnen neue Perspektiven auf österreichische Architektur im Spannungsfeld von Politik, Kultur und Globalisierung. Ein spannender Ausstellungstipp für alle, die Architektur, Geschichte und internationale Verflechtungen neu entdecken möchten. 🌏 #GlobalNeutral #Ausstellungstipp #Architekturgeschichte #staytuned #tbc --———— 🌍 GLOBAL – NEUTRAL. Architecture from Austria in Africa and Asia 1955–1989 Anne Wübben takes you on a short tour of the exhibition, exploring Austrian architecture in Africa and Asia during a period shaped by decolonisation, the Cold War and international exchange. Discover projects, photographs and models from the Az W collection and new perspectives on Austria’s global architectural connections. 🌏

candidateAudit.title: The second stage of our Coffee Journey is dedicated to the phase immediately following the harvest: extracting the bean from the coffee cherry. This operation must be performed pro
candidateAudit.text: The second stage of our Coffee Journey is dedicated to the phase immediately following the harvest: extracting the bean from the coffee cherry. This operation must be performed promptly, and there are two traditional methods to achieve this: wet processing and dry processing. It may seem like a minor detail, but the chosen method changes everything: the flavor, the aromas, and the body in the cup. Wet processing produces what are known as "washed" coffees and is the more complex of the two. The cherries are placed in water tanks; during this phase, light and immature cherries float to the surface, while the ripe, heavy ones sink to the bottom. They are then pulped and moved to fermentation tanks for up to 24 hours. This process highlights a coffee's acidity and its aromatic, citrusy, and floral notes. Dry processing is the method used for "natural" coffees. The cherries are spread out in the sun for 15–20 days and raked daily. During this time, the fruit pulp naturally transfers its sugars to the bean, imparting sweetness. Once dried, the coffee is hulled to remove the pulp and the parchment layer. This process enhances the coffee's inherent sweetness and creates a dense body. #goppioncaffe #bevilobuono #ilviaggiodelcaffe

candidateAudit.title: The journey of coffee to your cup is an exciting one. We’ve decided to tell this story starting right here: from the plantation and the harvest. There are three main harvesting tec
candidateAudit.text: The journey of coffee to your cup is an exciting one. We’ve decided to tell this story starting right here: from the plantation and the harvest. There are three main harvesting techniques: picking, stripping, and mechanical harvesting. At Goppion, almost all our coffees are harvested using the picking method. This involves hand-picking only the ripe cherries. Since this requires returning to the same plant multiple times throughout the season, it involves higher labor costs—which is why picking is reserved exclusively for high-quality coffees. Stripping, on the other hand, is still done by hand, but involves harvesting all the cherries in a single pass, regardless of their ripeness. The same principle applies to mechanical harvesting, which uses machines or manual shakers to speed up the process. #goppioncaffe #drinkgoodcoffee #thecoffeegourney #coffeelover

candidateAudit.text: Your Sportactivities: 📍 Location: Rahlgasse 5, 1060 Vienna 🗓 Every Monday: 15:00-22:00 🏋️‍♀️ Book: at Eversports->AuxGazelles In the heart of Vienna’s vibrant 1060, we’re rolling out mats, breaking a sweat, and finding calm in the motion every Monday at Aux Gazelles (Rahlgasse 5). 🧘‍♀️🏋️ Whether you’re bending into that warrior pose, powering through a sport-flow, or simply showing up to feel alive …. this is your invitation. Come as you are (yes, even if you think your mat skills are “beginner level”) … what matters is you showing up, breathing, stretching, connecting. Because yoga and sport aren’t about perfect form … they’re about movement, momentum, community. One breath at a time, one pose at a time, we tap into strength we didn’t know we had, we release the stories we’ve held, and we find the lightness in each muscle, each moment. From 15:00-22:00 every Monday, we transform Aux Gazelles into a space of motion and mindfulness. Expect: friendly smiles, real sweat, fresh energy, and a little bit of magic. Tag a friend who’s been saying “I’ll join next time” and let’s make it THIS Monday. The mat is ready. Are you? 🙏✨ #ViennaYoga #SportSessions #AuxGazelles #MondayMotivation

candidateAudit.text: 🍥bạn bánh mì #1 – akira_sugiura at Cà Phê Lalot🍥 “bạn” means friends in Vietnamese – and that’s the spirit of our new guest chef series “bạn bánh mì” where we invite chefs that we call friends to join us in the kitchen.
